notes.general: A son of Circe and Odysseus.
notes.here: He rules the Tyrrhenians with Latinus.

notes.label: Latinus
notes.general: A legendary ruler associated with the peoples of Italy.
notes.here: The son of Circe and Odysseus, described as noble and strong.

notes.label: Tyrrhenians
notes.general: A Greek name usually used for the Etruscans of ancient Italy.
notes.here: The people ruled by Agrius and Latinus in a distant island setting.

notes.label: Calypso
notes.general: An island goddess who shelters Odysseus during his travels.
notes.here: She bears him two sons.

notes.label: Nausithous
notes.general: A son of Calypso and Odysseus in this poem.
notes.here: The first of their two sons named.

notes.label: Nausinous
notes.general: A son of Calypso and Odysseus.
notes.here: Nausithous’s brother.

passages.title: The next song: mortal women
passages.summary: The list of divine mothers ends. The poet asks for a new song about mortal women.

verses.text: These were the goddesses who slept beside mortal men
and, though immortal, bore children like gods.
Now sing of the family of women, sweet-voiced
Muses of Olympus, daughters of Zeus who carries the aegis.

notes.label: Muses of Olympus
notes.general: The goddesses of song and poetry, daughters of Zeus.
notes.here: The poet asks them to begin the next subject.

notes.label: Aegis
notes.general: A divine shield or protective covering associated with Zeus.
notes.here: The closing line repeats Zeus’s title from the opening of this passage.

variants.title: Additional lines after verse 929
variants.summary: In this separate version, Hera bears Hephaestus without Zeus. Zeus swallows Metis, who conceives Athena inside him. Athena is born from his head, equipped for battle.

verses.label: 929a
verses.text: Hera grew furious and quarreled with her husband.

verses.label: 929b
verses.text: From this quarrel she bore a glorious son,

verses.label: 929c
verses.text: Hephaestus, without making love with Zeus, who carries the aegis,

verses.label: 929d
verses.text: whose skill with his hands surpassed that of all the heavenly gods.

verses.label: 929e
verses.text: But Zeus lay with the daughter of Oceanus and lovely-haired Tethys,

verses.label: 929f
verses.text: a girl with lovely cheeks, away from Hera,

verses.label: 929g
verses.text: deceiving Metis, though she knew so many tricks.

verses.label: 929h
verses.text: He seized her in his hands and put her inside his belly,

verses.label: 929i
verses.text: afraid she might bear another child stronger than his thunderbolt.

verses.label: 929j
verses.text: That was why Zeus, son of Cronus, enthroned on high and living in the upper air,

verses.label: 929k
verses.text: suddenly swallowed her. At once she conceived Pallas Athena,

verses.label: 929l
verses.text: whom the father of gods and humans brought to birth

verses.label: 929m
verses.text: from his head, beside the banks of the river Triton.

verses.label: 929n
verses.text: Metis stayed hidden beneath the organs inside Zeus’s body,

verses.label: 929o
verses.text: Athena’s mother, shaping what is right,

verses.label: 929p
verses.text: knowing more than all the gods and mortal humans.

verses.label: 929t
verses.text: With it, Zeus brought her to birth wearing her battle gear.

notes.label: Hera
notes.general: A goddess and Zeus’s wife.
notes.here: After quarreling with Zeus, she bears Hephaestus without him.

notes.label: Hephaestus
notes.general: The god of metalworking and skilled craftsmanship.
notes.here: Hera’s son, whose handiwork surpasses that of the other heavenly gods.

notes.label: Zeus
notes.general: The ruler of the gods, whose weapon is the thunderbolt.
notes.here: He swallows Metis and later gives birth to Athena from his head.

notes.label: Cronus
notes.general: Zeus’s father, who ruled the gods before him.
notes.here: The poem calls Zeus “son of Cronus.”

notes.label: Oceanus and Tethys
notes.general: Ancient water deities, parents of rivers and many goddesses.
notes.here: Their daughter is the woman Zeus sleeps with, apparently Metis.

notes.label: Metis
notes.general: A goddess of intelligence and cunning.
notes.here: Athena’s mother, who remains inside Zeus after he swallows her.

notes.label: Pallas Athena
notes.general: A goddess of wisdom, crafts, and warfare. Pallas is another name used for her.
notes.here: She is born from Zeus’s head wearing battle gear.

notes.label: Triton
notes.general: The name of a river whose location is uncertain.
notes.here: Athena’s birth takes place beside its banks.

notes.label: Olympus
notes.general: The mountain where the gods have their homes.
notes.here: The poem compares the goddess’s skill with that of all the gods living there.

notes.label: Aegis
notes.general: A divine protective covering, often pictured as a shield or cloak.
notes.here: The bracketed line describes it as Athena’s armor, terrifying enough to scatter armies.
